key_insight: Neutral ethylenediamine reconstructs tin-rich tin–lead perovskite surfaces toward stoichiometry, improving electron extraction and suppressing interfacial nonradiative recombination.
engineering_relevance: Controlling molecular protonation and surface defects offers a route to more efficient methylammonium-free perovskite solar cells.
method: Compare neutral ethylenediamine and protonated ethylenediammonium iodide surface treatments.
Use atomistic simulations to probe iodide migration and defect-assisted deprotonation.
Link surface reconstruction to electron extraction into C60 and solar-cell performance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 25.86% power conversion efficiency and simulations showing that subsurface iodide vacancies lower the energetic cost of deprotonation.
watch_item: Long-term stability and scalability of the surface treatment are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells
